back: N bonded to a C=O carbon: –CONH₂ (primary), –CONHR (secondary), –CONR₂ (tertiary).
Acid name -oic acid → -amide; groups on N shown with N-: CH₃CONHCH₃ = N-methylethanamide.
Acyl chloride + ammonia or a primary/secondary amine at room temperature (2 mol of the nitrogen compound).
LiAlH₄ in dry ether: RCONH₂ + 4[H] → RCH₂NH₂ + H₂O.

front: Why amides are very weak bases
back: The N lone pair is delocalised over the adjacent C=O group, so it is not available to accept H⁺.
Break the C–N bond: C=O side → acid (carboxylate in alkali); N side → amine/ammonia (ammonium salt in acid).
